In the main event of the evening, Adesanya will face Shara Magomedov in a five-round middleweight bout, while the co-headliner is a five-round welterweight matchup between Ian Machado Garry and Yaroslav Amosov.

Israel Adesanya Favored to Defeat Shara Magomedov at UFC Saudi Arabia

Per FightOdds.io, Adesanya is favored to beat Magomedov in the UFC Saudi Arabia headliner.

Israel Adesanya -205 Shara Magomedov +173

Adesanya is obviously the bigger name of the two fighters, and he has far more experience fighting in five-round UFC main events. But the former middleweight champ has lost four fights in a row and has been getting finished quite often as of late, having been stopped in his last three bouts.

As for Magomedov, he has won six of his seven fights in the UFC, and he is coming off back-to-back decision wins over Michel Pereira and Marc-Andre Barriault. He also possesses huge knockout power and has the ability to put anyone in the division away if he lands on their chin.

This UFC Saudi Arabia main event is a very intriguing fight, and could arguably be a must-win fight for Adesanya, as a fifth straight defeat could have him contemplating retirement from MMA.

Ian Machado Garry Favored to Beat Yaroslav Amosov

In the co-main event, Machado Garry is the favorite to beat Amosov.

Ian Machado Garry -185 Yaroslav Amosov +157

Machado Garry is coming off a disappointing decision loss to Islam Makhachev in a failed bid to become the new UFC welterweight champion at UFC 330, but he is still one of the best welterweights in the game today.

As for Amosov, he is 2-0 so far in the UFC with submission wins over Neil Magny and Joel Alvarez. If he can go in there and take out Machado Garry, there is a chance that Amosov could potentially get a UFC welterweight title shot in 2027.

articles.title: ‘More girls are coming forward’: Puja Tomar on MMA's growing popularity in India and what it will take to produce UFC fighters
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Puja Tomar remembers a time when MMA had little recognition in India.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Puja Tomar remembers a time when MMA had little recognition in India. Today, she sees more girls taking up the sport, more people following it and a growing interest in what happens inside the UFC Octagon. Having become the first Indian woman to win a fight in the promotion, Tomar wants to see that interest translate into opportunities for the next generation.The 32-year-old is in the spotlight again as part of the UFC India Tour, where she is looking forward to meeting fans and introducing more people to the sport.“It's amazing. I always dreamt of the things that I am experiencing today. I never thought MMA would grow so much in India. But after the UFC events and after winning fights, a lot of things have improved,” Tomar told TimesofIndia.com in an exclusive interaction on Saturday.She has noticed a change in the number of women taking up MMA since her UFC debut in June 2024, when she defeated Brazil's Rayanne dos Santos by split decision.“Earlier, there was hardly any awareness of MMA. Today, it has changed completely. It has become a trend, and everyone wants to take up MMA. Earlier, girls were unsure about whether they could do it, but now they are coming forward and doing well. A lot has changed,” she said.The gaps Indian MMA still needs to addressTomar has also seen the sport from the other side. Her experience competing internationally has given her an understanding of the preparation required to reach the UFC, and she believes Indian fighters need better support from the grassroots.“Things will have to change from the grassroots level. I've been involved in MMA for a long time, and over the years I've come to understand what is needed. We need international coaches, proper conditioning, the right kind of diet and proper guidance on weight cuts. These things are still lacking in many places in India,” she said.She believes more academies and gyms, with experienced coaches and fighters passing on their knowledge, could help address those shortcomings.“If more academies and gyms open in India, with international coaches and experienced fighters sharing their knowledge with young athletes, we can produce many UFC champions.”It is also the thinking behind her plan to start an MMA academy. Tomar wants to coach both men and women, but says she would particularly like to create an environment where more girls feel comfortable taking up the sport.“Sometimes, girls can find it difficult to feel comfortable in MMA. So, as a female coach, I would like to train more girls. Of course, I will train boys as well,” she said.Her own experience has given her a list of things she wants young fighters to have access to from the start.“There are many things that were missing during my own journey and caused delays, such as proper guidance, diet and learning how to work on an opponent. A lot of these things are still missing in India today. I am working towards it. And when the academy opens, I hope we can produce many UFC fighters and champions,” she said.Tomar would also like the UFC to play a role in building that infrastructure. She has a specific proposal: an academy where Indian fighters can train alongside UFC athletes.“Professional fighters don't get much support from the government. If there is a place where they can get everything they need right from the grassroots level, that would make a big difference,” she said.“I would like the UFC to plan something like opening an academy. UFC fighters should come and train our Indian fighters, and even spar with them. When Indian fighters get the opportunity to match their mental strength against these athletes, a lot of things can happen.”Two defeats, a family setback and a return to trainingTomar's own UFC career has had a difficult phase since that historic debut. She lost to Ireland's Shauna Bannon by second-round submission in March 2025, before China's Shi Ming submitted her in the first round of their Road to UFC bout in May 2026.The period after the fight against Shi was not straightforward either. Tomar had planned to return to training but a family situation forced her to put those plans on hold. Her mother was hospitalised for a month.“Soon after that fight, I was planning to return to training. But because of some family issues, I couldn't. My mother was in the hospital for a month, and that affected me a lot. I was very down during that period,” she said.Her mother is now doing well, and Tomar says she is preparing to return to training. She wants to work on the areas of her game that still need improvement, including wrestling and Jiu-Jitsu.“If you're in the UFC, you want to be a complete MMA fighter. You need to work on your ground game, wrestling and everything else. It's not that I haven't worked on these things since joining the UFC. I have worked on my wrestling and Jiu-Jitsu,” she said.“But there are still certain things and moments that you are unable to show inside the Octagon. I have worked on those areas, and I'm still working on them. I want to show what I'm capable of inside the Octagon. That's what I'm working towards.”She has not lost sight of the first victory that made her a UFC fighter, either. Tomar recalled the win over dos Santos as a moment she will never forget, and said the difficult fights that followed have also taught her lessons.“My life has changed a lot, and I'm living a very good life. When I got my first victory, it was an amazing moment that I will never forget. I created history,” she said.“In my second loss, I felt I was very close to winning that fight. But that's how I look at life: never give up. Never get demotivated. I always learn from my fights. If you want to stay in the UFC, every fight is tough, and every difficult fight teaches you something.”Asha Roka, Carlos Prates and the next Indian fighterAsked about Indian women who could follow her into the UFC, Tomar pointed to Asha Roka, whose striking she admires. Roka has a karate background, and Tomar said she had reached out to her after her own UFC debut victory.“Asha Roka, who comes from a karate background, has amazing striking. I called her after I won my first UFC fight. I told her that I look at her someone who has the potential to be in UFC. I think if she makes a comeback [to MMA], it will be easier for her to get a contract,” she said.Tomar is also looking forward to meeting Brazilian UFC fighter Carlos Prates, who is in India as part of the tour. She hopes established fighters can offer support and encouragement to Indian athletes trying to make their way into the promotion.“I'm excited to meet him. I want to talk to him about how he can inspire Indian fighters. He's a legend, and he should inspire our fighters. He should also support them. For a young fighter, that kind of support means a lot,” she said.For Tomar, the immediate task is to get back into the gym and prepare for another UFC fight. She is not treating two defeats as the end of her run in the promotion.“It's not as if I've lost two fights and that's the end of it. I'm turning that disappointment into motivation. Losing a fight is difficult. But if I win my next fight and become a champion, a lot of things will change. It will be like cricket. It will be a big thing,” she said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Trump shares cartoon of Dana White as press secretary
articles.summary: President Trump on Sunday shared a cartoon of Dana White, CEO and president of UFC, as White House press secretary after announcing that White had been proposed as a candidate for the role. The president posted a cartoon video with the same animation style as “Family Guy.” In the video, White is in the White…
articles.body:
President Trump on Sunday shared a cartoon of Dana White, CEO and president of UFC, as White House press secretary after announcing that White had been proposed as a candidate for the role.

The president posted a cartoon video with the same animation style as “Family Guy.” In the video, White is in the White House briefing room, standing at the podium and saying, “Trump made me press secretary, I brought help.”

Reporters in the audience then ask questions and UFC fighters that were standing alongside White at the podium attack them. The video also references comments made by fighter Josh Hokit after a bout at “UFC Freedom 250” on the White House lawn earlier this year, in which he said former first lady Michelle Obama is a man.

On Saturday, White said he will meet with Trump on Monday to talk about the president’s job offer for White House press secretary.

The UFC CEO told reporters in London that he was flying to Washington. He was also asked how he could handle multiple jobs at the same time, replying that he has “a lot of jobs already.”

“We have a meeting on Monday, so I’m sure I’ll have more to talk about after that,” White said.

Trump said Saturday that he offered the job of press secretary to White, writing in a Truth Social post that he asked White to bring “assistants” with him and named multiple UFC fighters.

“I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States,” Trump wrote. “I have requested that he bring with him assistants, even though some are not from our Country, of Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes, and Kayla Harris.”

“We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left. Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job!” he added.

articles.body:
For the first time since winning the gold medal at the 2024 Paris Olympics, Imane Khelif will be back in the ring.

As announced in a press conference on Friday, Khelif will return to Paris on Dec. 15 for a six-round professional fight against 21-year-old Dutch boxer Clarida Sarabia, who holds a 4-0 professional record.

"Days became weeks, weeks became months. I waited, doubted. But deep inside, the fire never died. Behind closed doors, I kept fighting," Khelif said ‌in ⁠the video posted by Stair Event on Instagram. "Because this fight was never only mine. It was for everyone who dared to be, for everyone who refused to give up."

articles.summary: Durante la velada de ayer se supo la cartelera del evento que se celebrará en Riyadh el próximo 5 de diciembre
articles.body: La UFC hizo oficial durante el día de ayer la cartelera al completo del UFC Arabia Saudí que se celebrará el 5 de diciembre en Riyadh, con varios combates que ya eran un secreto a voces. El mayor atractivo para el público español será el combate de Hecher Sosa ante Abdul Hussein, aunque también hay que destacar la pelea estelar entre Israel Adesanya (24-6) y Shara 'Bullet' Magomedov (17-1) y la co estelar entre Ian Garry (17-2) y Yaroslav Amosov (30-1). El combate entre Hecher y Hussein será el primero de todo el evento, por lo que será a una hora bastante temprana en España teniendo en cuenta que estas carteleras en Oriente Medio suelen celebrarse después de comer. Por otro lado, Adesanya buscará romper su mala racha en peso medio -cuatro derrotas consecutivas- ante uno de los prospectos más mediáticos de la división, que ha dejado mucho que desear en sus ultimas actuaciones. Aún así, el daguestaní sabe que una victoria ante el ex campeón le acercaría y mucho al cinturón. Eso sí, si 'The Last Stylebender' pierde su retirada estaría más cerca que nunca, ya que ha sido finalizado en sus últimos tres combates y es evidente que su mandíbula no es la misma de antes. De hecho, está siendo un final de carrera muy triste para uno de los GOATs de la categoría, que desde que perdió el cinturón ante Sean Strickland ha sufrido una dolorosa caída a los infiernos que cada día se agrava más. Lo que es de admirar es lo de Ian Garry. El pasado agosto, el peleador irlandés perdió contra Islam Makhachev su oportunidad de ser campeón de peso wélter en un combate muy disputado, y apenas cuatro meses después ha aceptado un combate contra un Yaroslav Amosov que es el 'coco' de la categoría y alguien al que nadie quería enfrentar. Amosov viene de someter a Joel Álvarez en mayo, y a pesar de acabar de entrar en el top 15 ya ha recibido una pelea que en caso de ganar le dejaría a las puertas del título. Su grappling es uno de los más peligrosos de la categoría, y ante 'The Future' tendrá una oportunidad de oro para ponerlo en práctica y demostrar que tras ser campeón en Bellator también tiene los suficiente para ser campeón en la UFC. Garry aceptó a finales de 2024 un combate en corto aviso contra Shavkat Rakhmonov, meses más tarde hizo lo propio ante Carlos Prates, y ahora ha hecho más de lo mismo ante el ucraniano. Un 'BMF' en toda regla. La cartelera también tendrá otros grandes nombres que convierten esta Fight Night en una de las mejores del año, tónica habitual cada vez que se visita Oriente Medio, aunque su celebración sigue siendo una incógnita. En un principio se iba a celebrar el día 28 de noviembre, pero se movió al 5 de diciembre por el conflicto bélico que se vive en Riyadh y las ciudades de la zona. Sin embargo, los bombardeos siguen sucediendo, por lo que habrá que cruzar los dedos para que la tensión se rebaje.
